title: Arsenal FC vs. Club Atlético de Madrid

eventMetadata.context_description: Arsenal's near-certain trader consensus in this UEFA Champions League semi-final second leg at Emirates Stadium stems from their home dominance and superior head-to-head edge, including a 4-0 league-stage rout of Atlético Madrid last October and a resilient 1-1 first-leg draw in Spain last week. Mikel Arteta's squad boasts key returns like Martin Ødegaard and Kai Havertz despite minor absences (Timber, Merino out), fueling momentum amid Premier League title contention, while Diego Simeone's visitors struggle with away knockout form. Atlético's set-piece threats via Griezmann or Álvarez, a Simeone masterclass, or an Arsenal red card could spark an upset, but current pricing reflects the Gunners' defensive solidity and crowd boost as decisive factors.

title: 2026 FIFA World Cup Winner

The primary resolution source will be official information from FIFA, however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: France's slight edge at 16.8% implied probability in trader consensus for the 2026 FIFA World Cup reflects strong March friendly wins over Brazil (2-1) and Colombia (3-1), underscoring squad depth amid a global injury crisis sidelining stars like Hugo Ekitike (Achilles). Spain (15.3%) trails closely, buoyed by Euro 2024 triumph and a manageable group featuring Cape Verde, Saudi Arabia, and Uruguay, though Lamine Yamal's hamstring tear raises concerns despite recovery progress. England (11.1%), Argentina, and Brazil (both 8.6%) remain competitive via talent pools and South American qualifying dominance—Argentina topped CONMEBOL with 38 points—but face absences like Rodrygo's ACL, Eder Militão's hamstring, and Argentina's Cuti Romero, compressing odds in the expanded 48-team format where group stage advancement favors upsets and parity persists into knockouts.

Leading the Premier League table, Arsenal contend with Martin Odegaard's ongoing knee issue and Bukayo Saka's ankle doubt ahead of their April 25 Newcastle clash, while Atletico sit fourth in La Liga amid a form dip—traders weigh home-soil resilience against Arsenal's attacking firepower and head-to-head edge.

title: Iran closes its airspace by...?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Iran initiates a major closure of its airspace, that is not solely due to weather conditions, by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A “major closure” is defined as a broad closure, cancellation, or suspension of commercial flights transiting, arriving in, and departing from Iranian airspace or a major Iranian Airspace region. A qualifying closure must apply generally to flights across Iran or a major Iranian airspace region. Limited cancellations, delays, or other partial closures will not qualify. Limited exceptions to a broad closure, however, will not disqualify such a closure from counting (e.g. exceptions for certain flights pre-approved by the Iranian Civil Aviation Authority may be permitted). 

Any non-weather complete suspension of commercial arrivals and departures affecting at least two of the following airports will qualify: Imam Khomeini International Airport (IKA), Mehrabad Airport (THR), Mashhad International Airport (MHD), Shiraz International Airport (SYZ), or Isfahan International Airport (IFN).

Qualifying previous examples include the January 2026 total closure of Iranian airspace except to international flights with express governmental permission (https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iran-shuts-airspace-most-flights-flightradar24-says-2026-01-14/) and the April 2024 closure of Iran’s western airspace (https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iranian-airports-cancel-flights-until-monday-morning-2024-04-14/). Non-qualifying examples include the January 27, 2026 partial closure of Iranian airspace around the Strait of Hormuz (https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/iran-issues-airspace-notice-for-military-drills-near-strait-of-hormuz/3812508) and the January 25 - April 25, 2026 VFR (Visual Flight Rules) flights suspension which did not broadly close commercial aviation in a qualifying region (https://www.intellinews.com/iran-suspends-general-aviation-and-vfr-flights-in-new-airspace-directive-421997/).

Warnings, No-Fly-Zones, or other flight restrictions imposed by airlines or countries other than Iran will not be sufficient for a “Yes” resolution.

Airspace closures which occur solely due to weather conditions will not qualify.

The primary resolution sources for this market will be official information from Iranian aviation authorities and a consensus of credible reporting.

Qualifying previous examples include the January 2026 total closure of Iranian airspace except to international flights with express governmental permission (https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iran-shuts-airspace-most-flights-flightradar24-says-2026-01-14/) and the April 2024 closure of Iran’s western airspace (https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iranian-airports-cancel-flights-until-monday-morning-2024-04-14/). Warnings, No-Fly-Zones, or other flight restrictions imposed by airlines or countries other than Iran will not be sufficient for a “Yes” resolution.

Airspace closures which occur solely due to weather conditions will not qualify.

The primary resolution sources for this market will be official information from Iranian aviation authorities and a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Amid the ongoing US-Iran-Israel conflict that erupted in late February 2026 with strikes on Iranian military targets, Tehran's airspace (OIIX FIR) remains closed to most international commercial flights, with only limited domestic operations and eastern transit corridors resuming in late April following a phased reopening plan. Iranian Civil Aviation Organization NOTAMs and advisories from EASA, US FAA, and EU states cite risks of misidentification by air defenses amid missile activity and retaliations. Over the past 24 hours, Iranian missile and drone attacks on UAE oil facilities in Fujairah prompted partial UAE airspace restrictions and IRGC alerts placing "Rastakhiz" missile bases on immediate retaliatory launch status, heightening fears of further escalation. Traders monitor for full closures—defined as broad suspensions affecting major airports like Tehran or Mashhad—precedents from January and March closures, and potential US strikes or Hormuz developments before key deadlines.

eventMetadata.context_description: Gavin Newsom leads trader consensus at 26% implied probability for the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination, outpacing Kamala Harris at 9% despite her edge in recent April polls like Harvard-Harris (50%) and RCP averages (28%), as bettors weigh her 2024 general election loss and approval challenges against Newsom's term-limited California governorship, national fundraising prowess, and established anti-Trump profile from high-visibility debates. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez trails closely at 8% buoyed by progressive youth support evident in Echelon and YouGov surveys, while Jon Ossoff (7%) and governors Josh Shapiro (5%) and Pete Buttigieg (5%) draw on swing-state appeal and communication skills. With a fragmented field ahead of 2026 midterms, consolidation could follow standout gubernatorial wins, Q2 fundraising reports, or DNC chair endorsements shifting momentum in battlegrounds.

eventMetadata.context_description: Vice President J.D. Vance holds a strong position as trader consensus favorite at 39% implied probability for the 2028 Republican presidential nomination due to incumbency advantages and alignment with President Trump's base, though recent stalled Iran negotiations and associated backlash have narrowed his lead amid geopolitical tensions. HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. tops markets at 49%, reflecting his high-profile MAHA movement challenging public health agencies, recent congressional hearings where he diverged from CDC guidance, and crossover appeal to populist voters despite past denials of a run. Secretary of State Marco Rubio's 21% odds have climbed on strong foreign policy showings, highlighting a contested post-Trump primary field ahead of 2026 midterms.

title: Eurovision Winner 2026
description:
This market will resolve to the country whose candidate for Eurovision 2026 wins.

If at any point it is impossible for the listed candidate to win Eurovision 2026 based on the rules of the competition (i.e. they are eliminated), this market may immediately resolve to "No".

If no winner is announced by July 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve "Other". All ties will be broken according to EBU's official Eurovision rules.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Eurovision (https://eurovision.tv/), including live footage of Eurovision 2026, however a consensus of credible reporting will suffice.

eventMetadata.context_description: Finland leads Polymarket trader consensus at 35% implied probability for Eurovision 2026 victory in Vienna, propelled by the buzz from Linda Lampenius and Pete Parkkonen's "Liekinheitin"—a striking classical-pop fusion with captivating first-rehearsal staging that topped the OGAE fan poll. Greece's Akylas follows at 18% with "Ferto," generating excitement via its innovative rotating-stage concept evoking video game worlds, as previewed in recent rehearsal photos. Denmark's Søren Torpegaard Lund holds third at 14%, buoyed by upgraded visuals and vocal prowess in rehearsals for "Før Vi Går Hjem." Australia's Delta Goodrem and France round out frontrunners amid all 35 songs released, with semi-finals looming May 12-14 heightening televote and jury speculation.

eventMetadata.context_description: The Cleveland Cavaliers visit the Detroit Pistons for Game 1 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals on May 5 in Detroit, a Central Division rivalry renewed in the playoffs. Both squads advanced from first-round wins—Detroit via a gritty defensive effort against Orlando, highlighted by Cade Cunningham's playmaking and Jalen Duren's rim protection—entering with clean injury reports except Pistons wing Kevin Huerter (questionable, left adductor strain). Cleveland's healthy frontcourt duo of Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen poses matchup challenges to Detroit's physicality, while home-court advantage and recent momentum shape trader consensus on a tightly contested series opener amid rapid lineup updates.

title: Next French Presidential Election
description:
The next French presidential election is currently expected to be held around April 2027.  This market pertains to the outcome of the next French presidential election, regardless of whether it follows the scheduled end of the current term or is held earlier. 

The President of France is elected via a two-round system; a candidate must secure over 50% of the vote to win outright in the first round. If no candidate achieves this, the top two contenders advance to a runoff.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins this election.

This market includes any potential second round. If, for any reason, the results of the election are not known by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the French Government, specifically the Ministry of the Interior (https://www.interieur.gouv.fr/).

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on the 2027 French presidential election reflects a tight first-round race led by Rassemblement National president Jordan Bardella at 23.5%, buoyed by recent opinion polls showing him topping voting intentions around 40-42% amid widespread desire for change following March municipal elections where far-right made gains without major city wins. Former Prime Minister Édouard Philippe, at 20.5%, trails closely as Horizons leader and Le Havre mayor, bolstered by polls positioning him as the strongest second-round challenger against Bardella, often winning head-to-heads by slim margins. Ongoing political fragmentation since 2024 snap legislative elections, multiple government collapses, and undecided party primaries keep the field crowded and probabilities dispersed; candidate declarations, economic shifts, or scandals could widen leads ahead of April 2027 voting.

title: LoL: Hanwha Life Esports vs DN SOOPers (BO3) - Esports World Cup Korea Qualifier Playoffs
description:
This market refers to the LoL Upper bracket quarterfinal 1 match between Hanwha Life Esports and DN SOOPers in the Esports World Cup Korea Qualifier Playoffs, initially scheduled for May 5 at 4:00AM ET.

This market will resolve to "Hanwha Life Esports" if Hanwha Life Esports win the match against DN SOOPers.

This market will resolve to "DN SOOPers" if DN SOOPers win the match against Hanwha Life Esports.

If the match is canceled (not played at all), ends in a tie, or is delayed beyond 7 days from the scheduled date without a winner determined, this market will resolve to 50-50. 

If the match begins but is not completed, and one team wins due to the opponent's forfeiture, disqualification, or walkover, this market will resolve to the team who wins. 

If the match ends in a forfeit, disqualification, or walkover (team withdraws before the start and the other wins automatically), this market will resolve to 50-50. 

The resolution source for this market will be official information from https://gol.gg/esports/home. However, if https://gol.gg/esports/home has not published final results within 2 hours after the event’s conclusion, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead including video evidence.

In cases where a team’s listed name includes minor discrepancies from the resolution source, this market will resolve based on the underlying real-world match rather than exact name matching. Recognizable abbreviations, alternate or erroneous spellings, sponsor tags, affiliate or academy designations, regional identifiers, and minor formatting differences will be treated as referring to the same team, provided the intended team can be clearly and uniquely identified within the relevant competition. If a listed team name has no reasonable connection to any participating team, or if it matches or could reasonably refer to another team in the same competition such that the intended team cannot be unambiguously determined, this market will resolve 50-50.

markets.question: Game 1: Any Player Quadra Kill?
markets.description:
This market is about whether any player achieves a Quadra Kill during Game 1. In League of Legends, a Quadra Kill occurs when a single player kills 4 enemy champions in rapid succession.

markets.question: Game 3: Any Player Quadra Kill?

markets.question: Game 3: Odd/Even Total Kills?

This upper bracket BO3 pits LCK elite against struggling underdogs, with HLE's meta dominance and momentum driving trader favoritism amid no reported roster shifts.

title: Elon Musk # tweets May 1 - May 8, 2026?
description:

markets.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (HIGH) $150 in May?
markets.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation during May 2026, any 1-minute candle for the Active Month of WTI Crude Oil futures has a final "High" price equal to or above the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No". 

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

Only prices achieved during the applicable trading session for the underlying market will be considered. Under the standard schedule, trading is open from 6:00:00 PM ET Sunday through 5:00:00 PM ET Friday, with a daily break from 5:00:00 PM ET to 6:00:00 PM ET, except where modified by holiday or special-session hours. 

Per CME contract specifications for WTI Crude Oil (CL) futures, a contract’s last trading day is three business days prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract's delivery month (or four business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a business day).

The active month changes at the start of the second trading session prior to the nearest listed contract’s last trading session. At that point, the next listed contract becomes the active month (i.e., for the final three trading sessions of the nearest listed contract, the contract for the next month is the active month). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 6:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date.

For example, if the 25th of the month is a Saturday, the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Tuesday the 21st, and the next listed contract becomes the active month at the start of the trading session for Friday the 17th (6:00 PM ET on Thursday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other technical disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil (CL) futures contract by CME Group may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session.

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the Active Month WTI Crude Oil futures "High" prices available at https://pythdata.app/explore?search=WTI, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation during May 2026, any 1-minute candle for the Active Month of WTI Crude Oil futures has a final "High" price equal to or above the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No". 

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

Only prices achieved during the applicable trading session for the underlying market will be considered. Under the standard schedule, trading is open from 6:00:00 PM ET Sunday through 5:00:00 PM ET Friday, with a daily break from 5:00:00 PM ET to 6:00:00 PM ET, except where modified by holiday or special-session hours. 

Per CME contract specifications for WTI Crude Oil (CL) futures, a contract’s last trading day is three business days prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract's delivery month (or four business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a business day).

The active month changes at the start of the second trading session prior to the nearest listed contract’s last trading session. At that point, the next listed contract becomes the active month (i.e., for the final three trading sessions of the nearest listed contract, the contract for the next month is the active month). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 6:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date.

For example, if the 25th of the month is a Saturday, the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Tuesday the 21st, and the next listed contract becomes the active month at the start of the trading session for Friday the 17th (6:00 PM ET on Thursday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other technical disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil (CL) futures contract by CME Group may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session.

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the Active Month WTI Crude Oil futures "High" prices available at https://pythdata.app/explore?search=WTI, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

eventMetadata.context_description: WTI crude oil spot prices closed at $102.68 per barrel on May 5, 2026, down 3.5% amid profit-taking after intraday highs near $105, pressured by OPEC+'s decision to raise May production quotas by 206,000 barrels per day. EIA's latest Short-Term Energy Outlook projects Brent peaking at $115/b in Q2 2026 before easing, with WTI futures for May 2026 trading around $92 amid a backwardated curve reflecting near-term tightness. Key catalysts include weekly EIA inventory reports, geopolitical risks in the Strait of Hormuz, and OPEC+ compliance through month-end.

eventMetadata.context_description: Vice President JD Vance leads trader consensus at 20.2% implied probability for the 2028 presidential election winner, buoyed by his position as heir apparent in a Trump administration and strong showings in early GOP straw polls like CPAC's March survey where he garnered 53% support. California Governor Gavin Newsom trails closely at 17.1%, reflecting his national profile as a leading Democratic contender amid party soul-searching post-2024, reinforced by recent youth polling favoring him alongside Kamala Harris. Secretary of State Marco Rubio at 10.9% gains from high-profile foreign policy roles in Venezuela and Iran, positioning him as a GOP alternative. This tight race persists due to the early stage before 2026 midterms, which could elevate governors like Newsom or Josh Shapiro through electoral performance, while scandals, Trump endorsements, or primary announcements might create separation among the fragmented field.

title: US x Iran permanent peace deal by...?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Iran and the United states agree to a permanent peace deal by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”. 

A permanent peace deal refers to any agreement which explicitly indicates that military hostilities between the United States and Iran have ended or will permanently cease, or uses equivalent language clearly signaling a lasting end to military hostilities between the United States and Iran. Agreements that are explicitly temporary or which do not include a definitive agreement to end military hostilities between the US and Iran on a lasting basis (e.g. a temporary extension of the two-week ceasefire agreement announced on April 7, 2026), will not qualify.

A qualifying agreement will be considered to have been established if either of the following conditions are met:

- The United States and Iran each sign or formally adopt a written agreement (e.g. a treaty or multi-point agreement) which meets the above criteria.

- Both the governments of the United States and Iran provide clear public confirmation that a qualifying agreement has been definitively established. Negotiations, statements of progress, or other statements which do not constitute a definitive announcement that a qualifying agreement has been reached will not count.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Ongoing indirect US-Iran negotiations, mediated by Pakistan, continue amid a fragile ceasefire in place since early April 2026, following collapsed direct talks in Islamabad and a US naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz imposed after April 12. Iran submitted its latest peace proposal two days ago—responding to a US nine-point plan calling for nuclear suspension and sanctions relief—while President Trump's administration reviews it, demanding verifiable limits on uranium enrichment and ballistic missiles before any permanent deal. Sticking points include Hormuz access and sequencing of nuclear talks. Traders weigh diplomatic momentum from proposal exchanges against escalation risks, with potential second-round talks looming and Iran's 30-day review possibly delaying progress before June deadlines.

title: UEFA Champions League Winner
description: This is a polymarket to predict which club will win the 2025–26 UEFA Champions League (soccer).

markets.question: Will Real Madrid win the 2025–26 Champions League?
markets.description:
This is a polymarket on whether the listed team will win the 2025–26 UEFA Champions League.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if the listed team is officially crowned the winner of the 2025–26 UEFA Champions League. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No".

If at any point it becomes impossible for the listed team to win the tournament (e.g. they are mathematically eliminated), the market will resolve to "No".

If the 2025–26 UEFA Champions League is canceled or not completed by October 1, 2026, this market will resolve to "Other".

The primary resolution source will be official information from UEFA Champions League (https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/). A consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Arsenal leads trader consensus at 40.5% implied probability to win the UEFA Champions League, buoyed by a resilient 1-1 away draw in their semifinal first leg against Atletico Madrid last week and upcoming home advantage in the second leg on May 5, underscoring their defensive solidity amid a grueling knockout path that saw them dispatch Sporting CP in the quarterfinals. Bayern Munich holds 30.5% following a dramatic 4-5 loss to PSG in the other first-leg thriller but leverages prolific scoring form—highlighted by knocking out Real Madrid—and a home second leg on May 6 to overturn the aggregate deficit. PSG. PSG. PSG. PSG. PSG sits at 28.5% with a slim lead yet exposed defensive frailties in the high-scoring encounter, while Atletico Madrid and Club Brugge languish at 0.1% after earlier eliminations. These positioning stem from last week's semifinal openers and teams' knockout momentum.

title: Will __ ships transit the Strait of Hormuz on any day by end of April?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if IMF Portwatch publishes a daily number of transit calls (“Arrivals of Ships”) for the Strait of Hormuz equal to or above the listed value for any date between market creation and April 30, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The number of daily transit calls/arrivals includes container, dry bulk, roll-on/roll-off, general cargo, and tanker ships. Ships not reported by IMF Portwatch will not be considered.

This market will resolve as soon as IMF Portwatch publishes a daily number of transit calls equal to or above the specified level, or once data has been published for the final date in the specified period and no such value has been published. If no data has been published for the final date of the specified period within 14 calendar days (ET) after the end of that period, this market will resolve based on data published up to that point.

Revisions to previously published data points, made within this market’s timeframe, will be considered. However, they will not disqualify a previously published data point from qualifying. Revisions to previously published data points after data is published for April 30, 2026, however, will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market will be IMF Portwatch, specifically the transit calls data published for the Strait of Hormuz at https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/cb5856222a5b4105adc6ee7e880a1730, both in the chart and through downloadable files.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket reflects deeply discounted probabilities for elevated ship transits through the Strait of Hormuz by April 30, 2026, driven by reciprocal U.S.-Iran blockades initiated April 13 amid escalating conflict. IMF Portwatch data confirms daily arrivals cratered to 4-12 vessels in late April—versus pre-war norms of ~100—following Iranian seizures of containerships on April 22 and sporadic attacks, slashing volumes by over 90%. This impasse has embedded a 20-30% geopolitical risk premium into Brent crude, now above $110/bbl, while VLCC tanker rates on Baltic Exchange routes like TD3C have surged amid war risk insurance hikes. U.S. "Project Freedom" escorts enabled two U.S.-flagged transits post-deadline, but UN sanctions proposals and ceasefire talks loom as key catalysts.

eventMetadata.context_description: Former Health Secretary Xavier Becerra holds a slim trader consensus edge over billionaire Tom Steyer in the 2026 California gubernatorial race, driven by Becerra's surge in late April and early May polls tying him atop the primary field at 23-24% alongside Republican Steve Hilton, following his strong April 22 debate performance and Rep. Eric Swalwell's withdrawal that consolidated Democratic support. Steyer counters with unmatched self-funding—poised to make this the costliest primary—and fresh endorsements from progressive groups like Our Revolution, keeping the contest neck-and-neck amid voter concerns over affordability and the economy. California's top-two primary on June 2 could advance two Democrats to November, amplifying the stakes; late endorsements, final polls, or turnout in diverse battlegrounds like Los Angeles and the Central Valley may create separation before ballots drop.

title: Strait of Hormuz traffic returns to normal by May 15?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls (“Arrivals of Ships”) for the Strait of Hormuz equal to or above 60 for any date between market creation and May 15, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Daily transit calls include container, dry bulk, roll-on/roll-off, general cargo, and tanker ships. Ships not reported by IMF Portwatch will not be considered.

This market will resolve as soon as IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls equal to or above the specified level, or once data has been published for the final date in the specified period and no such value has been published. If no data has been published for the final date of the specified period within 14 calendar days (ET) after the end of that period, this market will resolve based on data published up to that point.

Revisions to previously published data points made within this market’s timeframe will be considered. However, they will not disqualify a previously published data point from qualifying. Revisions to previously published data points after data is published for May 31, 2026, however, will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market will be IMF Portwatch, specifically the transit calls data published for the Strait of Hormuz at https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/cb5856222a5b4105adc6ee7e880a1730, both in the chart and through downloadable files.

eventMetadata.context_description: Ongoing Iranian restrictions and recent US-Iran military clashes, including US Apache helicopters destroying six Iranian fast-attack boats on May 4 and a cargo ship attack near the strait on May 3, have kept commercial shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz at just 10-20% of normal levels—around 9-11 vessels daily versus the typical 60. Since late February, Iran has limited passage to pre-approved vessels amid a fragile ceasefire, with US-led blockades and elevated insurance risks trapping dozens of ships and prompting major carriers to suspend routes. Trader consensus at 98% "No" reflects no de-escalation signals, stalled diplomacy, and predictions of prolonged disruption into summer. A sudden bilateral ceasefire or UN-brokered agreement could shift odds, though structural tensions persist.

title: Trump announces US blockade of Hormuz lifted by...?
description:
On April 12, 2026, President Donald Trump announced that the United States will blockade the Strait of Hormuz. You can read more about that here: https://www.nbcnews.com/world/iran/live-blog/live-updates-us-iran-fail-reach-deal-peace-talks-day-negotiations-rcna315918.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if President Trump, the US government, or the US military publicly and officially announces the end of the United States blockade of the Strait of Hormuz by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

Qualifying statements must clearly and explicitly indicate that the United States has lifted, ended, or will lift or end its blockade of the Strait of Hormuz on a specified date or use equivalently definitive language unambiguously signaling that such blockade has ceased or is set to cease on a specified date (e.g., statements unambiguously indicating that US naval activity in the relevant area has ceased will qualify). 

Statements that merely describe actions inconsistent with the blockade (e.g., "Iran resumed shipping through the Strait of Hormuz") without explicitly indicating the blockade as lifted will not alone suffice.

Informal announcements, statements from unnamed sources, or leaks do not qualify.

Written public statements from Donald Trump (e.g., posts from his personal Truth Social account) will qualify. Videos posted on his social media accounts will also qualify for a "Yes" resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official statements from the US government and/or its official representatives; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

Note: this market will resolve solely based on whether a qualifying announcement is made within the specified timeframe. Whether the blockade is effectively enforced or whether maritime traffic resumes absent a qualifying announcement will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: President Trump's US naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, imposed April 13 after failed Iran nuclear talks, remains firmly in place amid mutual naval posturing and mine threats. Over the past week, Iran launched attacks on US ships, prompting Trump to terminate a brief truce citing unmet demands, while the Pentagon disclosed a six-month timeline for mine clearance. Launched Sunday, Project Freedom aims to escort stranded vessels but has not eased restrictions, fueling global gas price surges past $4.50 per gallon. No lifting announcement has occurred; traders monitor diplomatic breakthroughs, escalation risks, or looming War Powers Resolution deadlines that could force congressional intervention or policy shifts.

title: Fed Decision in June?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's June 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for June 16-17, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their June meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

This skin-in-the-game positioning aligns closely with CME FedWatch probabilities near 95%. Realistic challenges include a sharper-than-expected April CPI drop on May 12 or weakening May jobs data ahead of the meeting, potentially prompting a 25 basis point cut reassessment.

title: US x Iran diplomatic meeting by...?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a diplomatic meeting between representatives of the United States and Iran by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A diplomatic meeting refers to a deliberate meeting between representatives of the listed countries who are acting in an official capacity and are authorized to engage in negotiation or diplomacy regarding US-Iranian relations on behalf of their governments. Meetings conducted indirectly, for example, through designated mediators, facilitators, or interlocutors acting with the knowledge and authorization of the relevant governments, will qualify. 

Brief greetings, chance encounters, or talks otherwise not deliberately aimed at diplomacy or negotiation will not count. 

The meeting must be in-person and must be publicly acknowledged by either government or reported by a consensus of credible media. Remote meetings, phone calls, or other meetings where the relevant parties are not present will not count.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran, and a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Amid a fragile ceasefire in the 2026 Iran conflict, US-Iran indirect diplomacy has regained momentum with recent backchannel exchanges, as US envoy Steve Witkoff confirmed Washington is in conversation with Tehran while Iran reviews America's response to its three-stage peace proposal. President Trump expressed skepticism, calling the offer likely unacceptable amid core sticking points including Iran's nuclear enrichment, ballistic missiles, Strait of Hormuz access, and sanctions relief. Last month's direct talks in Pakistan ended without agreement, fostering trader consensus of low implied probability for a qualifying high-level diplomatic meeting by June 30 despite mediator efforts by Pakistan and Oman. Potential escalation or breakthroughs in ongoing negotiations could sway outcomes.

title: Internazionali BNL d'Italia: Martina Trevisan vs Talia Gibson
description:
This market refers to the tennis match between Martina Trevisan and Talia Gibson in the Internazionali BNL d'Italia, originally scheduled for May 5, 2026 at 5:00AM ET.

This market will resolve to 'Martina Trevisan' if Martina Trevisan advances against Talia Gibson.

This market will resolve to 'Talia Gibson' if Talia Gibson advances against Martina Trevisan.

If the match is canceled (not played at all), ends in a tie, or is delayed beyond 7 days from the scheduled date without a winner determined, this market will resolve to 50-50.

If the match begins but is not completed, and one player advances due to the opponent's retirement, default, or disqualification, this market will resolve to the player who advances.

If the match ends in a walkover (player withdraws before the start and the other advances automatically), this market will resolve to 50-50.

The primary resolution source will be official information from the WTA Tour. A consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Talia Gibson enters as the trader consensus favorite against Italian wild card Martina Trevisan in the Internazionali BNL d'Italia Round of 128 on clay, fueled by her breakout 2026 hard-court surge—QF at BNP Paribas Open (upsetting No. 7 Jasmine Paolini, No. 11 Ekaterina Alexandrova) and R16 at Miami Open (edging No. 15 Naomi Osaka)—despite a modest 0-2 clay record from recent R1 Madrid loss to Emiliana Arango and R32 Saint-Malo exit. Trevisan, ranked No. 516 with a 5-3 YTD clay mark from ITF semifinals in Santa Margherita di Pula, leverages home-crowd support and historical clay prowess (former Rabat champion), though her 0-8 Rome record and recent Madrid qualifying defeat signal vulnerability. No head-to-head; stylistic clash pits Gibson's power against Trevisan's baseline grinding amid outdoor conditions.

In Dota 2, a "kill" for markets like team total kills, kill handicap, and interval kills is counted when an enemy hero dies and the game awards a hero kill event to the opposing team's score, which is the number shown on the in-game scoreboard and tracked in scoreboard feeds as team kills. In practical terms, this includes any enemy hero death that increments a team's kill score, regardless of who got the last hit, including situations where the victim dies to creeps, a tower, or neutrals as long as the kill is still credited to the enemy team. It does not include denies, such as killing your own allied units, and it also does not include building or objective destructions like towers, barracks, or Roshan, since those are tracked separately from kills. Assists also do not count as kills, because they are recorded as a separate player stat and multiple players can assist on a single kill.

This market is about the total kills in Game 2.

This market will resolve to "Over" if the total kills in Game 2 is 52 or more. Otherwise, it will resolve to "Under".

If the match is canceled (not played at all) or is delayed beyond 7 days from the scheduled date, this market will resolve to 50-50.

If Game 2 is never played due to forfeit, disqualification, or walkover, this market will resolve to 50-50.

If Game 2 begins but is not completed, this market will resolve to 50-50.

If Game 2 is remade, resolution will be based on the total kills in the remade game only.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from https://www.dotabuff.com. However, if https://www.dotabuff.com has not published final results within 2 hours after the event’s conclusion, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead including video evidence.


In Dota 2, a "kill" for markets like team total kills, kill handicap, and interval kills is counted when an enemy hero dies and the game awards a hero kill event to the opposing team's score, which is the number shown on the in-game scoreboard and tracked in scoreboard feeds as team kills. In practical terms, this includes any enemy hero death that increments a team's kill score, regardless of who got the last hit, including situations where the victim dies to creeps, a tower, or neutrals as long as the kill is still credited to the enemy team. It does not include denies, such as killing your own allied units, and it also does not include building or objective destructions like towers, barracks, or Roshan, since those are tracked separately from kills. Assists also do not count as kills, because they are recorded as a separate player stat and multiple players can assist on a single kill.

eventMetadata.context_description: In 1win Essence I Group B's best-of-three clash, REKONIX holds a dominant 4-1 head-to-head edge over Team Nemesis, reflecting their established Southeast Asian roster—Jikroy on carry, inYourdreaM mid, Fbz offlane, dalul support, and Varizh hard support—stable since mid-2025. Nemesis fields a freshly assembled lineup with rubikon155 (Pos 1), 4nalog (Pos 2), captain Jabz (Pos 3), Lelis (Pos 4), and Yamsun (Pos 5), all joined in late April, plus new coach Astini, amid integration challenges after a 0-2 loss to Nigma Galaxy. REKONIX sits 1-1 in the group (2-0 over L1GA Team, 1-2 to Zero Tenacity), while standings pressure mounts for playoff spots on patch 7.41b's scaling meta.
